HOW: only release when the failure happened before commit — e.g. track a committed flag, or move free() outside the try and guard it separately so a free() failure does not release a hold that is already committed.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim is technically correct per the code and interface docs. In changeSeat, commit(hold) runs at line 26 inside the try, then free() at line 27 can throw; the catch at line 30 calls release(hold) on a hold that was already committed. Since holds never expire and only commit()/release() end them, releasing a committed hold leaves the new seat (booking keeps newSeatId) unprotected, and the vacated booking.seatId is never freed and stays blocked. The failure path is concrete and reachable. This is not a repeat of the earlier hold-leak decision: that entry described a leaked hold (seat blocked), whereas this describes the inverse — an over-release of a committed hold plus an un-freed seat — a different consequence arising from applying the earlier fix.

delivered.text: A failing `free()` releases an already-committed hold, so the booking keeps `newSeatId` while its hold is gone, the seat the user vacated is never freed, and the seat stays blocked for everyone since holds never expire. Only release the hold when the failure happened before `commit` — track a `committed` flag or move `free()` outside the `try` and guard it separately.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the 429 and 5xx retry branches are still unreachable because `if (status >= 400) return { kind: 'drop', ... }` (line 12) is evaluated before `status === 429` (line 13) and `status >= 500` (line 14), so those two checks only run for statuses that are neither 2xx nor >= 400 (i.e. <200 or 300–399). WHY: every 429 and every 5xx still returns 'drop', so transient failures are dead-lettered instead of retried and the delivery is permanently lost, contradicting the comment above the function. This is the same failure the earlier suggestion about this branch described; the applied change moved the code into a discriminated union but did not reorder the checks, so the defect remains. HOW: move the 429/5xx checks above the `>= 400` check (the final `return` already drops every other non-2xx status), e.g. keep the 2xx delivered check first, then the 429 and 5xx retry checks, and leave a single trailing drop return.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The technical claim is factually correct (line 12 `status >= 400` runs before the 429/5xx checks, making them unreachable). However, this is the exact failure already raised in PreviousDecision round-a-P38-unreachable-retry-reintroduced (same file src/webhooks/outcome.ts, same unreachable-retry/429-and-5xx-dead-lettered problem, outcome "implemented"). The finding itself acknowledges it is "the same failure the earlier suggestion about this branch described." Raising the same problem (same failure: transient 429/5xx dead-lettered instead of retried) that already has a comment on this PR is a repeat, so it must be dropped per the dedup rule.
